justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: R-01 via Claim Submission UI Module, R-02 via Adjuster Workspace UI Module, and R-03 via Claim Routing Engine, Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer - ACL, and Mainframe Message Translator with Versioning & Feature Flags.
justifications.performance_efficiency: R-05 is directly addressed using Claim Caching & Read Model Component (CQRS-lite read models), Response Caching Component in APIM, asynchronous processing via Azure Service Bus, and ADF parquet staging to meet the tight nightly batch window.
justifications.compatibility: Integration with the legacy DB2/COBOL mainframe is robustly modeled using Mainframe Integration Adapter, IBM MQ / CICS Client, and ADF Self-Hosted Integration Runtime (SHIR) Cluster. Azure Active Directory integration supports enterprise identity standards.
justifications.usability: Distinct web portals serve both user groups via dedicated React modules (Claim Submission UI Module and Adjuster Workspace UI Module). However, broker-specific workflows or specialized portal customization details remain generic.
justifications.reliability: R-04 (zero data loss) is satisfied with Outbox Pattern Processor, Duplicate Detection Filter, Azure Service Bus FIFO sessions, Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager, ADF Reconciliation & Error-Handling Pipeline, and Dead Letter Manager Component.
justifications.security: R-07 is satisfied via Authentication Client Module and JWT Validation Policy with Azure AD. Additionally, Database Security & Auditing, Row-Level Security, TDE, and Audit Repository Access Component ensure confidentiality, integrity, and traceability.
justifications.maintainability: R-06 (reverting within one day) is supported via Claim Routing Engine, feature flags in Mainframe Message Translator, and Mainframe Anti-Corruption Layer. The architecture has clean modular boundaries and loose coupling via Azure Service Bus.
justifications.portability: The hybrid environment (on-premise and Azure West Europe) is supported through Azure Container Apps and ADF SHIR. However, deep coupling to proprietary Azure PaaS services (APIM, Service Bus, ADF) limits multi-cloud or cloud-agnostic portability.

PERF-01.justification: The architecture decouples UI reads from slow mainframe queries using CQRS-lite read models, Redis caching in API Management and the Claims Core Service, and background staging tables populated by asynchronous ETL syncs.
elements: Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs
sensitivity_points: Cache hit ratios for claim lookups
Read model staleness versus consistency requirements
tradeoffs: Caching improves latency but introduces eventual consistency across read models

PERF-02.justification: Submissions are accepted asynchronously via API Management, buffered in Azure SQL Database and Azure Service Bus, and staged via Azure Data Factory, completely protecting the mainframe batch window from online peak load.
sensitivity_points: Queue ingestion capacity and broker throughput
Blob staging and database write performance during load surges
tradeoffs: Buffering requests guarantees availability during peaks at the cost of delayed mainframe processing

AVAIL-01.justification: The Outbox Pattern Processor, Mainframe Sync Queue, and Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager absorb online submissions during the batch window outage, deferring mainframe dispatch without dropping any transactions.
sensitivity_points: Capacity and retention limits of Service Bus queues during downtime
Outbox processor backoff and retry scheduling
tradeoffs: Asynchronous outbox dispatch preserves availability while introducing temporary reconciliation lag

AVAIL-02.justification: Service Bus Duplicate Detection, FIFO sessions, transactional outbox persistence, and Azure Data Factory reconciliation pipelines explicitly ensure idempotent delivery, state reconciliation, and zero data loss or duplicate processing.
sensitivity_points: Message deduplication time windows in Service Bus
Mainframe sequence tracking across interrupted synchronization jobs
tradeoffs: Strict FIFO ordering and deduplication overhead reduce peak synchronization throughput

MOD-01.justification: The Claim Routing Engine, APIM routing policies, and the Mainframe Message Translator with feature flags permit instantaneous cutover or 1-day rollback per claim type without modifying client interfaces or legacy schemas.
elements: Mainframe Message Translator with Versioning & Feature Flags
sensitivity_points: Centralized configuration management for dynamic feature toggles
Completeness of the anti-corruption layer schema mapping
tradeoffs: Maintaining dual routing and translation paths increases architectural complexity temporarily

MOD-02.justification: The frontends interface solely with the modern API layer and Claims Core Service. Decommissioning the mainframe only requires repointing routing policies and retiring the integration adapter and ACL, preserving all UIs unchanged.
elements: Customer Portal and Adjuster Workspace SPAs
sensitivity_points: Elimination of legacy data model dependencies within the domain model
Migration completeness of historical claim archives to Azure SQL
tradeoffs: Strict façade abstraction shields UIs but adds indirection layers throughout the migration

SEC-01.justification: Security is addressed with JWT validation at the gateway, Azure SQL Row-Level Security, and dedicated audit pipelines. However, specific authorization policies enforcing broker tenant isolation are not explicitly defined in the domain service.
sensitivity_points: Enforcement of tenant isolation in API policies and domain logic
Completeness of security logging and audit trail persistence
tradeoffs: Enforcing row-level security and auditing adds processing overhead to database queries

SEC-02.justification: Centralized SSO via Azure AD ensures credential revocation propagated through OpenID Connect. However, without explicitly configured short-lived tokens or Continuous Access Evaluation, standard JWT lifespans may exceed the 15-minute revocation requirement.
sensitivity_points: Token expiration lifespans and JWKS cache invalidation frequency
Support for Continuous Access Evaluation or proactive token blacklisting
tradeoffs: Shorter token lifetimes guarantee faster revocation but increase token refresh traffic
